BIEN1010.d: This course is designed as an introductory course in biomedical engineering. The aim of this course is to present some of the basic science and human physiology knowledge used by biomedical engineers and illustrates the first steps in applying this knowledge to solve problems in human medicine. The second goal of this course is to link knowledge of basic science and engineering to fields of specialization and current research. This course also introduces the sub-specialties in biomedical engineering and through real-life examples to emphasize the types of problems biomedical engineers solve.
cl: Summarize the key points of the areas in bio/medical engineering and demonstrate the applications of these areas in our daily life
Explain how to apply the engineering principles in solving bioengineering problems in daily life by showing examples
Explain why it is important for bioengineers to understand the human body
Critique the medical technologies in the markets based on your knowledge in bioengineering
Evaluate the social, ethical and economic impacts of innovations/technologies in bio/medical engineering
Demonstrate you are a good team player and presenter

BIEN1600.d: This course provides an overview and lays the foundation for the bioengineering discipline. Students will delve into diverse topics such as biomaterials, biosensors, tissue engineering, and bioimaging. Through lectures with case studies, students will analyze the design and development of technological advances in healthcare and life science, including biomolecular tools, medical devices, and regenerative medicine applications.
cl: Understand the foundational principles of bioengineering, including the integration of engineering concepts with biological systems.
Analyze and evaluate various bioengineering topics such as biomaterials, biosensors, tissue engineering, and bioimaging.
Apply knowledge gained to design and develop innovative solutions in healthcare, including medical devices, biomolecular tools, and regenerative medicine applications.
Evaluate and discuss the ethical implications and societal impact of bioengineering advancements in healthcare practices.
Develop the ability to address complex healthcare challenges in a team using bioengineering principles and interdisciplinary collaboration.

BIEN1610.d: This course offers an introductory overview of synthetic biology and its innovations for human health, encompassing both technical and business aspects, tailored for undergraduate students. It is suitable for those intrigued by the cutting-edge technologies driving the emerging biopharmaceutical industry and interested in the transformation of synthetic biology. This course begins by exploring the timeline of biotechnology's emergence and development, delving into the discovery of groundbreaking pharmaceuticals in human history and the evolution of synthetic biology. It provides students with a framework for critical thinking while exploring the current landscape of synthetic biology. The course covers key milestones, explains foundational scientific concepts, and highlights the transformative impact of synthetic biology on human health. Through case studies, students gain insights into the opportunities and limitations in current and future technological advancements. Additionally, the course features guest lectures by experts from the industry and investment sector, offering valuable perspectives on course-related topics.
cl: Explain the basic technical concepts, scientific and engineering principles in medical synthetic biology
Describe the opportunities and challenges facing the synthetic biology industry
Analyze the potential and impact of synthetic biology on human health and bioeconomy
Identify the key components that contribute to commercially relevant synthetic biology
Work in a team with complementary strengths
Communicate technical ideas clearly and effectively to diverse audiences
Evaluate personal interests in synthetic biology and the broader biotech industry through reflection on the course project

BIEN1620.d: This course offers a comprehensive introduction to biomedical engineering, equipping students with foundational knowledge in basic sciences and human physiology. Key topics include bioinstrumentation, where students explore techniques for measuring physiological parameters such as temperature, blood pressure, and blood composition. The bioimaging segment covers advanced imaging modalities like MRI, CT, and ultrasound, which are vital for diagnostic applications. In biomolecular engineering, students will learn about the working principles and development history of vaccines, antibodies, innovative drug delivery systems, and various gene editing technologies. Additionally, the course also introduces bioinformatics, focusing on genomic sequencing and its significance in modern healthcare. Throughout the course, an engineering and user-centered design approach will guide students, emphasizing the importance of creating solutions that prioritize patient needs and real-world applications. This blend of theory and practical experience prepares students to tackle challenges and fosters an appreciation for the evolving field of biomedical engineering.
cl: Describe key concepts in biomedical engineering and illustrate their applications in everyday life
Apply engineering principles to solve biomedical engineering problems, supported by relevant examples from personal experiences
Describe essential human anatomy and physiology relevant to biomedical engineering professionals
Critically assess current medical technologies in the market, leveraging knowledge of biomedical engineering principles
Evaluate the social, ethical, and economic implications of innovations and technologies in biomedical engineering
Demonstrate effective teamwork and presentation skills, showcasing the ability to collaborate and communicate ideas clearly

BIEN2310.d: Modeling of physical, chemical and biological processes. Balance Equations. Dimensional and scaling analysis. Analytical and numerical solutions to initial and boundary value problems. Use of computer tools for engineering calculations. This course uses examples in the Bioengineering discipline. For BIEN students only.
cl: Model simple physical, chemical and biological processes as mathematical equations.
Develop and interpret differential equations in initial and boundary value problems.
Solve differential equations analytical and/or numerically.
Describe elementary concepts in statistics and perform simple hypothesis testing and regression analysis.
Use computing tools for engineering calculations.

BIEN2410.d: Essential cellular and systems physiology for engineers. Hierarchical organization of a complex organism: from organelles to organ systems. Cellular physiology, neurophysiology, vision, muscle and movement, and the cardiovascular system.
cl: Describe the essential concepts in cell biology and systems physiology.
Describe the principles of the neural and cardiovascular systems.
Appreciate the connection between cellular and systems physiology and the design and engineering of pharmaceutical products and biomedical devices.
BIEN2410.pq: LIFS 1901 OR Level 3 or above in HKDSE 1x Biology

BIEN2610.d: A concise introduction of biochemistry, cell biology, and pharmacology to engineers. Molecular and supramolecular building blocks of biological systems. Analysis and engineering of biological systems by chemical principles. Introduction to transcriptomics, proteomics and metabolomics.
cl: Describe at a basic level the biochemical machinery of living cells.
Describe and apply analytical techniques for biomolecules, including omics.
Describe techniques and application of biomolecular engineering.
Describe concepts in basic pharmacology and drug discovery.
Apply concepts in chemistry to evaluate innovative ideas in bioengineering.
BIEN2610.pq: (CHEM 1010 (prior to 2022-23) OR CHEM 1012) AND (LIFS 1901 OR (Level 3 or above in HKDSE 1x Biology))

2540.pq: (CHEM 1010 OR CHEM 1012) AND (LIFS 1901 OR (Level 3 or above in HKDSE 1x Biology))

2530.pq: (CHEM 1010 OR CHEM 1012) AND (LIFS 1901 OR (Level 3 or above in HKDSE 1x Biology))

2520.pq: (CHEM 1010 OR CHEM 1012) AND (LIFS 1901 OR (Level 3 or above in HKDSE 1x Biology))

BIEN2990.d: For students in the Bioengineering major. This course is designed to provide academic advising to students, to enhance their understanding of the bioengineering field, to encourage them to pursue co-curricular learning opportunities available to them, and to improve their communication skills. Students are required to attend discussion sessions with advisors and fellow students and selected workshops and seminars. Graded P or F.
cl: Be motivated and equipped to pursue the co-curricular learning opportunities available to bioengineering students.
Be aware of possible career paths of bioengineers and how to prepare for them.
Form a strong community with faculty and fellow students in the program.
Communicate effectively in group settings.

BIEN3250.d: Analysis of transport phenomena and rate processes, including fluid flow, energy and mass transport, and reactions in biological systems. Applications in human physiology, bioreactors, medical devices, drug delivery, and biosensors. Mathematical and computational tools for solving problems and designing applications involving such processes.
cl: Describe the fundamental principles of transport phenomena and reaction kinetics.
Describe and model rate and transport processes in biological systems.
Formulate and solve problems involving rate and transport processes.
Appreciate the connection between rate and transport processes and animal physiology and how it influences the effective design of various biomedical devices.
Use computing tools for problem solving involving rate and transport processes.

BIEN3300.d: This course is an introductory course on the application of machine learning methods in molecular engineering problems. It covers fundamental data processing and machine learning methods to analyze data in chemistry and biology such as molecular similarity calculation and property prediction.
cl: Identify problems that can be formulated as a supervised learning task.
Process different types of data to be ready for model training.
Understand the principles of supervised learning methods.
Perform model training, validation and testing.
Clearly interpret model predictions and present model results.
Know the application of data science methods in molecular science related problems.

BIEN3310.d: This is an introductory course on data science and its applications in neural engineering. The course introduces the fundamentals of data science, principles of  neuroscience, and the technologies and implementations of neural engineering. The  topics include probability, random variables, statistical detection and estimation, random process, structure and function of the nervous system, encoding and  decoding, population coding, neural network, plasticity and learning, neural interfaces and rehabilitation.
cl: Understand the basic concepts of probability, random processes, expectation and averages.
Obtain a holistic view of neural engineering.
Recognize the neuroanatomy and understand the basic functions.
Comprehend fundamentals of basic coding theory and computation methods.
Analyze neural data and implement on neural-controlled device/robot.
Enhance the knowledge in neural engineering, signal processing and practical programming.
BIEN3310.pq: (CENG 2310 OR ELEC 2600 OR LIFS 3150 OR MATH 2411) AND (BIEN 3300 OR CENG 3300 OR MATH 2111)

2540.pq: (BIEN 2310 OR ELEC 2600 OR ELEC 2600H (prior to 2022-23) OR MATH 2111) AND (BIEN 3300 OR CENG 3300 OR LIFS 3150 OR MATH 2411)

2530.pq: (BIEN 2310 OR ELEC 2600 OR ELEC 2600H (prior to 2022-23) OR MATH 2111) AND (BIEN 3300 OR CENG 3300 OR LIFS 3150 OR MATH 2411)

2520.pq: (BIEN 2310 OR ELEC 2600 OR ELEC 2600H (prior to 2022-23) OR MATH 2111) AND (BIEN 3300 OR CENG 3300 OR LIFS 3150 OR MATH 2411)

BIEN3320.d: This is an introductory course for the application of data science in biology and medicine. The course will introduce the fundamental principles on data science, the technologies and implementations of data mining, as well as the modeling of several practical questions in biomedicine. The topics include introduction to biomedical data, data visualization, regression methods and classification methods.
cl: Obtain a basic understanding of data science as a discipline.
Understand high-throughput biomedical data of various types.
Visualize, analyze and interpret biomedical data with sound statistical principles.
Apply computational methods and software tools in data science in the context of biomedicine.
Develop mathematical models for scientific questions.
BIEN3320.pq: (COMP 1021 OR COMP 1023) AND (level 3 or above in HKDSE 1x Biology OR LIFS 1901)

2540.pq: {COMP 1021 OR [(COMP 1022P OR COMP 2011) AND COMP 1029P]} AND (LIFS 1901 OR level 3 or above in HKDSE 1x Biology)

2530.pq: {COMP 1021 OR [(COMP 1022P OR COMP 2011) AND COMP 1029P]} AND (LIFS 1901 OR level 3 or above in HKDSE 1x Biology)

2520.pq: {COMP 1021 OR [(COMP 1022P OR COMP 2011) AND COMP 1029P]} AND (LIFS 1901 OR level 3 or above in HKDSE 1x Biology)

BIEN3410.d: This course introduces various bioimaging methods and their data analysis approaches, including optical coherence tomography, fluorescence microscopy, nonlinear microscopy, super-resolution microscopy, ptychographic microscopy, and photoacoustic tomography. Students will be able to understand, design, and evaluate those imaging techniques. This course requires basic knowledge of linear algebra, calculus, and geometry.
cl: Describe the working principles of widely used bioimaging technologies.
Design and evaluate bioimaging devices that can acquire biological information from the human body.
Describe how bioimaging technologies address biological and clinical needs in practice.
Research and evaluate information about bioimaging technologies and their applications.

BIEN3420.d: This course will cover the fundamental principles in bioinstrumentation and biosensing devices, and practical examples of such in biomedical applications. Concepts in bioelectric and biochemical signals, their measurement and transduction will be introduced.
cl: Describe the working principles of widely used bioinstrumentation and biosensors.
Design and evaluate bioinstrumentation and biosensors that can acquire bioelectrical or biochemical signals from the human body.
Describe how bioinstrumentation and biosensors address clinical needs in practice.
Appreciate how technological advances in this field can potentially revolutionize healthcare in the future.

BIEN3910.d: This course provides hands-on experience with molecular biotechnology, biomolecular engineering, biosensors, biomedical devices, and bioanalytical techniques. Laboratory experiments including cell culture, genetic engineering techniques, bioanalytical methods, biosensors and biomedical devices, with additional emphasis on data analysis. For students of the CBE department only. May be graded PP.
cl: Describe the principles behind the experimental modules and how they are applied in the experiments (tentatively molecular biotechnology, biomaterials, biosensors, sequencing and bioimaging).
Design and conduct experiments relevant to the bioengineering discipline.
Process, analyze and interpret experimental data in a statistically sound manner.
Develop soft skills including teamwork, open-ended problem solving, report writing and presentation.

2540.d: This course provides hands-on experience with molecular biotechnology, biomolecular engineering, biosensors, biomedical devices, and bioanalytical techniques. Laboratory experiments including cell culture, genetic engineering techniques, bioanalytical methods, biosensors and biomedical devices, with additional emphasis on data analysis. For students of the CBE department only.

2530.d: This course provides hands-on experience with molecular biotechnology, biomolecular engineering, biosensors, biomedical devices, and bioanalytical techniques. Laboratory experiments including cell culture, genetic engineering techniques, bioanalytical methods, biosensors and biomedical devices, with additional emphasis on data analysis. For students of the CBE department only.

2520.d: This course provides hands-on experience with molecular biotechnology, biomolecular engineering, biosensors, biomedical devices, and bioanalytical techniques. Laboratory experiments including cell culture, genetic engineering techniques, bioanalytical methods, biosensors and biomedical devices, with additional emphasis on data analysis. For students of the CBE department only.

BIEN4000.d: Selected topics of current interest not covered by existing courses. May be graded by letter, P/F, or DI/PA/F for different offerings.
cl: Equip with broad and useful knowledge to various topics which are not covered by existing courses.
(Each offering under the umbrella will have specific learning outcomes.)

BIEN4110.d: This course aims to introduce basic concepts of regulatory science, while familiarizing students with product development, manufacturing, medical and engineering operations, and quality control / quality assurance processes in the pharmaceutical and medical device industry. Students will also be introduced to the associated regulatory requirements, with an emphasis on Hong Kong, Great Bay Area, China and beyond, in topics such as Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP), pharmaceutical product registration, pharmacovigilance, and clinical trials.
cl: Form a conceptual framework of regulatory science and engineering that underpins regulatory affairs of medical products worldwide.
Outline the current practices of medical and engineering operations in the pharmaceutical and medical device industry.
Describe the importance and processes of quality assurance / quality control in the manufacture of both pharmaceutical products.
Outline how Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) and Pharmaceutical Inspection Convention and Pharmaceutical Inspection Co-operation Scheme (PIC/S) are implemented.
Outline the roles of medical affairs, medical science liaison, and pharmacovigilance in the pharmaceutical industry.
Describe the principles and practice of clinical trials and the importance of clinical trials in drug development.

BIEN4910.d: Independent studies or projects under the directed guidance of a faculty member on a bioengineering topic. Enrollment in the course requires prior approval of the course instructor, and credits assigned depend on the workload. Students may repeat the course if different topics are taken. The course may be grade by letter or P/F subject to different offerings. May be graded PP.
cl: Learn the professional and technical knowledge in the bioengineering research area.
Equip students with written and presentation skills in engineering disciplines.

BIEN4920.d: A final-year project course offers practice of bioengineering design through a group design project chosen to integrate materials covered in the curriculum. Credit load may be spread over a year. May be graded PP. For students in the Bioengineering major only.
cl: Integrate and synthesize the knowledge they learned in various courses in the curriculum.
Design and conduct wet-lab or dry-lab experiments to optimize and evaluate designs.
Design processes or products in the realm of bioengineering creatively to meet societal needs.
Function effectively in multi-cultural and multi-disciplinary teams.
Articulate the problem being solved and the solution provided by the design effectively both in writing and orally.
Evaluate the impact of bioengineering design on contemporary society from various pertinent perspectives.
Research and evaluate information related to bioengineering, and use it effectively in their own design.
Manage a project effectively by proper work allocation and personal management, and setting and meeting appropriate goals and deadlines.

BIEN4930.d: A final-year project course offers an opportunity to conduct individual bioengineering research under the direct supervision of a faculty member, which leads to a Bachelor's thesis. Credit load may be spread over a year. May be graded PP. For students in the Bioengineering major with approval from the department only.
cl: Manage a research project effectively by personal management and setting and meeting appropriate goals and deadlines.
Obtain and evaluate information related to bioengineering, and use it effectively in their own research.
Evaluate the impact of bioengineering research on contemporary society from various pertinent perspectives.
Articulate research questions and outcomes effectively both in writing and orally.
Function effectively in multi-cultural and multi-disciplinary teams.
Conduct scholarly research in the realm of bioengineering.
Design and conduct wet-lab or dry-lab experiments.
Integrate and synthesize the knowledge they learned in various courses in the curriculum.

BIEN4940.d: This course is intended to provide final-year bioengineering students with practical hands-on training in the form of a full-time or part-time internship or co-op program in a bioengineering company. Credit load may be spread over a year. May be graded PP. For students in the Bioengineering major with approval from the department only.
cl: Integrate and synthesize the knowledge they learned in various courses in the curriculum.
Design and conduct wet-lab or dry-lab experiments to optimize and evaluate designs.
Design processes or products in the realm of bioengineering creatively to meet societal needs.
Function effectively in multi-cultural and multi-disciplinary teams.
Articulate the problem being solved and the solution provided by the design effectively both in writing and orally.
Evaluate the impact of bioengineering design on contemporary society from various pertinent perspectives.
Research and evaluate information related to bioengineering, and use it effectively in their own design.
Manage a project effectively by proper work allocation and personal management, and setting and meeting appropriate goals and deadlines.

BIEN4990.d: For final-year Bioengineering students. This course is designed to prepare students for the workplace, to instill in them a sense of professional responsibility, and to enhance their career management skills. Students are required to attend selected workshops and seminars by practicing bioengineers. Graded P or F.
cl: Understand the career opportunities available to bioengineering graduates.
Approach the job search process with preparedness and confidence.
Function effectively in the workplace as a professional.
Appreciate the standard of ethics and professional responsibility expected of bioengineers.

BIEN5010.d: The course introduces the basics of cell biology, molecular biology techniques, and discusses the principles of macromolecular interactions in those contexts. We will also discuss various applications of these techniques and how combined with engineering concepts, they have contributed to innovations and breakthrough tools in the world of basic research and medicine. Topics to cover include: overview of basic molecular biology and macromolecular interactions; basic biophysical structures, imaging and characterization techniques; molecular engineering; biodevices; and genomics. Active student discussion is required and students will also do a final project team presentation on a current bioengineering topic.
cl: Describe the central dogma of molecular biology, and be able to recall the various molecular components (molecules, proteins/enzymes) involved in the components of the central dogma. Describe their main physical features and select appropriate tools/techniques for characterizing them.

Explain the mechanisms and functions of basic molecular biology assays, including PCR, qPCR, gel electrophoresis, molecular cloning, protein separation and purification; be able to analyze and interpret results of above assays.
Compare different types of imaging tools, and describe their usage and importance in modern biotechnology/medicine.

Explain what a stem cell is, and compare differences between embryonic stem cells, fetal stem cells, adult stem cells, and induced pluripotent cells; recall modern applications of stem cell therapies, and explain the mechanism of action for these therapies; describe current major challenges in using stem cell therapies in the clinic.

Explain and critique recent breakthroughs in molecular biology and bioengineering fields, including those outside your research area; be able to suggest potential applications of these new technologies to a relevant clinical challenge.

Present and discuss the taught ideas and concepts with peers with clarity and evidence-based reasoning; collaborate with team mates with positive attitude and strong work ethic in a group project setting.

BIEN5040.d: This course will provide a survey of Neuroscience and Neuroengineering research areas to provide our research postgraduate students a broad appreciation of interdisciplinary research in context. The course aims to help student recognize and understand how knowledge from science and engineering interface in this interdisciplinary application. Concepts such as neural interfacing and neural prosthesis will be introduced so that students can understand the impact of the latest technologies. The course will enhance the vision of the students and encourage them to work in future inter-disciplinary research fields.
cl: Obtain a holistic view of systems neuroscience fundamentals and methods.
Recognize the neuroanatomy and understand the basic functions.
Write a literature review on a topic within systems neuroscience.
Explain basic neural coding theory and computation method.
Enhance the knowledge in related area, such as neural engineering.

BIEN5050.d: Through real-time videoconferencing with participants from different countries such as the United States, United Kingdom, Australia, Mexico, and Philippines, this ONLINE course aims at helping students learn the definitions of global health ethics and bioethics, the different protocol and systems in place to ensure adherence to ethical principles, and how different stakeholders and cultures may interpret ethics differently. Through case studies on ethical challenges from real-world situations, students will analyze and discuss the complexities of global health practice and research ethics in a global context. This course is co-offered with the University of Southern California. Besides the joint LIVE sessions, face-to-face sessions and group projects are also arranged for the introduction of background knowledge, case studies, group project discussion, and technical support.
cl: Articulate the important ethical considerations of biomedical research, basic and clinical, involving human subjects.
Outline the unique ethical and social implications of conducting such research in developing countries of different economic status.
Identify key trends and emerging issues in global health ethics.
Analyze situations of ethical challenges in global health practice and research from diverse perspectives.
Appreciate the role culture and religion play in the development of a sense of right and wrong and views on ethics and how protocol fitting to the local context can be justified
Describe best practices in ethical health research and practice to protect human subjects and their legal right

BIEN5060.d: The course will introduce the basic concepts in detection of biosignals. Students will learn about the biosensing components, transduction mechanisms, novel materials in sensing, and analytical techniques to capture diverse health information. The course will also touch upon the physical and chemical sensors used for healthcare applications. We will also discuss about the emerging flexible, wearable technology toward personalized healthcare. Students will have opportunities to design and propose biosensors and bioelectronics at the end of the course.
cl: Explain how biosensors work.
Describe different techniques for bio-signal determination.
Evaluate biosensors performance.
Propose biosensors for real world applications.

BIEN5070.d: Synthetic biology, which echoes the assertion “What I cannot create, I do not understand” made by Richard Feynman, has been hailed as a revolution for modern science and technology. Unfledged as it is, the field, arising from the synergistic combination of chemistry, biology, engineering, data science, and information/control theory, has already shown great promise in addressing energy and health-related global challenges. This course aims to expose students with diverse backgrounds to this highly interdisciplinary field and furnish them with necessary guidance and ideas for taking on synthetic biology projects.
cl: Describe the basic concepts and engineering principles in synthetic biology.
Describe the central dogma of molecular biology and control strategies of gene replication, transcription, post-transcriptional modification, and translation.
Describe the genetic parts, devices, circuits, and systems in synthetic biology.
Explain the design of genetic circuits, including genetic input, biological computing, and output Modules, and describe what Design–Build–Test–Learn (DBTL) cycle is in synthetic biology.
Explain the mechanisms of synthetic biology tools, including Gibson assembly, Golden Gate assembly, DNA recombination, DNA synthesis, directed evolution, and genome editing.
Recognize, evaluate, and criticize the design of genetic circuits in scientific literature of synthetic biology.
Explain real-world applications of synthetic biology.
Enhance communication skills.

BIEN5080.d: This course provides graduate students with a fundamental and integrated understanding of core principles in thermodynamics, chemical reaction kinetics, and transport phenomena, with applications to chemical and biological systems. It equips students - particularly those without prior chemical engineering training - with quantitative reasoning tools to interpret equilibrium and dynamic processes in biological and physiological systems. Through in-class discussions, homework, and student presentations, the course applies these principles to address research questions and practical challenges in bioengineering and related fields.
cl: Apply fundamental principles of thermodynamics, chemical kinetics, and transport phenomena to analyze equilibrium and dynamic processes in chemical and biological systems.
Use quantitative engineering tools to interpret exemplary biological and physiological phenomena mechanistically.
Critically evaluate and solve research-oriented problems in chemical engineering and bioengineering through in-class discussions and applications.
Communicate technical concepts effectively via presentations and written summaries.
Collaborate in teams to apply course knowledge to design projects addressing practical or research challenges in biological systems.

BIEN5820.d: Introduction to Microfluidics and Biosensors; Overview of microfabrication materials & techniques; microfluidic principles; miniaturized biosensors; micro total analysis system (µTAS) & lab-on-a-chip (LOC) for clinical and research applications.
cl: Describe core concepts in the field of Microfluidics & Biosensors.
Describe trends and motivations in the field of Microfluidics & Biosensors.
Analyze/critique research articles in the field of Microfluidics & Biosensors.
Formulate a potential solution for a clinical problem using Microfluidics & Biosensors.

BIEN6800.d: Seminar topics presented by students and faculty. Students are expected to attend regularly and demonstrate proficiency in their seminar presentation in accordance with the program requirements. Graded P or F.
cl: Identify current research of interest in various topics of bioengineering.
Obtain insights to how peer researchers design and conduct experiments.
Gain opportunities to make academic and social contacts with the peer researchers.
Demonstrate proficiency in presentation of research outcome coherently and thoroughly (as presenters).

BIEN6810.d: Bioengineering Colloquia is a seminar course that brings prominent researchers in the field of bioengineering to share their research with BIEN colleagues and students. The course aims to provide a platform for discussions and exchange of ideas on the late advancements in the field of bioengineering. Students will have the opportunity to engage with the speakers and ask questions, fostering a deeper understanding of the research presented. The course will cover a broad range of topics, including chemical engineering, biotechnology, material sciences, synthetic biology and more. Students are expected to attend regularly. Grade P or F.
cl: Gain a comprehensive understanding of the latest advancements and research trends in various areas of bioengineering.
Develop the ability to critically analyze and evaluate research presentations, recognizing the significance and implications of the findings.
Improve their ability to articulate questions and engage in discussions, enhancing their communication skills in a professional setting.
Appreciate the interdisciplinary nature of bioengineering by exploring topics across chemical engineering, biotechnology, material sciences, and synthetic biology.
Learn how to network effectively with professionals and researchers, building connections that may benefit their academic and career pursuits.
Develop informed perspectives on current challenges and future directions in the field of bioengineering.

BIEN6910-6940.d: Selected topics in bioengineering of current interest in emerging areas and not covered by existing courses. May be repeated for credit if different topics are covered. May be graded by letter or P/F for different offerings.
cl: To demonstrate a capability to integrate knowledge and to analyse, evaluate and manage the different aspects of a special topic in bioengineering.

BIEN6990.d: Master's thesis research supervised by a faculty member.  A successful defense of the thesis leads to the grade Pass.  No course credit is assigned.
cl: To demonstrate a capability to research and development work.
To demonstrate the capability to create, analyse and critically evaluate different technical solutions.
To demonstrate the capability to critically and systematically integrate knowledge.
To demonstrate the capability to clearly present and discuss the conclusions as well as the knowledge and arguments that form the basis for these findings in written and spoken English.
To demonstrate a consciousness of the ethical aspects of research and development work.

BIEN7990.d: Original and independent doctoral thesis research.  A successful defense of the thesis leads to the grade Pass.  No course credit is assigned.
cl: To demonstrate a capability to research and development work
To demonstrate the capability to create, analyse and critically evaluate different technical solutions.
To demonstrate the capability to critically and systematically integrate knowledge.
To demonstrate the capability to clearly present and discuss the conclusions as well as the knowledge and arguments that form the basis for these findings in written and spoken English.
To demonstrate a consciousness of the ethical aspects of research and development work.
